The use of blackface in the US was recorded through “minstrel shows,” in which white performers would wear blackface and mock Black people.The Halloween costume controversy comes nearly a year after Target rolled back Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) initiatives.Chief merchandising officer of Target Cara Sylvester sent an internal email in which the employees were told that the iten should never have been in the assortment and that the company would learn from this and do better.
Article Summary: The $25 costume was listed as the “Kids’ Glows under Blacklight Circus Clown Halloween Costume Bodysuit” from Target’s Hyde & EEK! Boutique line. The design featured an orange-and-black clown outfit, black gloves and a dark face covering.

Article Title: In 1957, Georgia artist Eddie Owens Martin began transforming his inherited farmhouse and seven acres; 29 years of work created six major structures and 900+ feet of painted walls, now preserved as on
Article Text:
Georgia artist Eddie Owens Martin

From fortune teller to Georgia visionary

Decay leads to major restoration

Preserving Pasaquan for the future

In 1957, eccentric folk artist Eddie Owens Martin returned to his rural roots near Buena Vista, Georgia, and began turning a seven-acre family property into a colourful world of painted totems, geometric designs and tall masonry walls. Over the next 29 years, Martin, who called himself "St. EOM", built six major structures and more than 900 feet of brightly painted walls. The site became what is now considered one of North America's most important visionary art environments. Known as Pasaquan, a name Martin created to mean "the past coming together", the site combines Mesoamerican designs, African patterns, Eastern symbols and futuristic ideas into a highly personal style.Born in 1908 to a family of rural Georgia sharecroppers, Martin left home for New York City at 14. He spent the next three decades working in the city's nightlife and later became a professional fortune teller. According to biographical records maintained by Columbus State University, Martin experienced powerful spiritual visions while seriously ill in 1935. He said a futuristic being told him to change his life and follow "Pasaquoyanism", a personal spiritual system that linked growing long hair with spiritual energy, harmony with the universe and artistic creation."You're gon' be the start of somethin' new, and you'll call yourself Saint EOM, and you'll be a Pasaquoyan, the first one in the world," Martin recalled of the vision, according to statements preserved by the Pasaquan Preservation Society. After his mother's death, Martin returned to Marion County in 1957 and began building his vision on the family property. He funded the work through fortune telling and tarot readings for local residents. Without formal architectural plans, he spent decades constructing concrete buildings, circular dance platforms, two-storey pagodas and detailed shrines. "I built this place to have somethin' to identify with, 'cause there's nothin' I see in this society that I identify with or desire to emulate," Martin said in archival interviews preserved by the John Michael Kohler Arts Center.Martin died in 1986. Local supporters then formed the Pasaquan Preservation Society to protect the unusual site. Despite their efforts, years of extreme weather, high humidity and termite damage badly affected the painted walls and wooden structures. Pasaquan was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2008, recognising its importance as a major example of outsider art. But the site still faced serious physical damage. In late 2013, preservation leaders turned to the Wisconsin-based Kohler Foundation after deciding that a full restoration was beyond the resources available locally. The foundation took responsibility for the site in 2014 and began one of the most complex efforts to restore an American art environment. The two-year project involved specialist conservators from Parma Conservation in Chicago, International Artifacts in California and regional construction teams. Workers repaired damaged masonry foundations, treated extensive termite damage, removed overgrown vegetation and carefully repainted deteriorating surfaces. Historical photographs were used to match the bright colours and designs created by St. EOM.After the restoration was completed in 2016, the Kohler Foundation donated the seven-acre Pasaquan site to Columbus State University (CSU), securing its future as a public and educational site. Today, Pasaquan is managed through the university's Department of Art. It operates as an educational centre, museum and residency site for visiting artists from around the world. Most of St. EOM's outdoor sculptures and painted walls remain at the original site in Marion County. Some of his paintings, textiles and jewellery are also held in permanent collections at CSU and the John Michael Kohler Arts Center, helping protect his work from potential natural disasters. Pasaquan remains open for self-guided tours, educational programmes and cultural events. The colourful complex stands as a lasting record of Martin's 29-year effort to create his own alternative world from concrete, paint and personal belief.
Article Summary: Eddie Owens Martin spent 29 years turning a Georgia property into a colourful world of painted totems, geometric designs and tall masonry walls. Known as Pasaquan, a name Martin created to mean "the past coming together", the site combines Mesoamerican designs, African patterns, Eastern symbols and futuristic ideas into a highly personal style. The site is now considered one of North America's most important visionary art environments.

Article Title: Foreign students must make an official request for authorization: ICE issues new memo as colleges pause CPT program; American students will also have to complete training
Article Text:
ICE explains why CPT is not meant for only international students.

How is CPT defined in regulation?

How is CPT different from Optional Practical Training?

Can CPT be offered as a part of an elective course?

Because CPT is allowed only where the training is an integral part of an established curriculum, does that mean that all students enrolled in the established curriculum must participate in and complete practical training?

Are foreign students required to proactively request CPT authorization from their DSO?

Must all CPT be conducted by sponsoring employers that have established cooperative agreements with the school?

As US universities started pausing CPT (Curricular Practical Training), which is a temporary work authorization for F-1 students, triggering confusion over the future of international students in the US, Immigration and Customs Enforcement issued another memo clarifying and doubling down on the new restrictions. CPT allows F-1 students to gain off-campus work experience, internships, before graduating and hence it has to be related to the student's major. For approval of these internships, students do not have to go to immigration; the university itself can approve them. ICE said the university administration is not giving these approvals judiciously.On August 12, ICE issued a directive to all schools and universities stating that CPT has to be an integral part of the course. Many universities, including UC Berkeley, UC Davis, UC San Diego, Purdue, Santa Clara paused the approvals of CPT programs.In the new memo, ICE explained some of the frequently asked questions and made it clear that all students attending the same course must do CPT as it must be mandatory. American students, too, will have to do this, otherwise it's not valid because it's not mandatory then.A foreign student may be authorized by a DSO (Designated School Official) to participate in a CPT program that is an integral part of an established curriculum.Curricular practical training is defined as alternative work/study, internship, cooperative education or any other type of required internship or practicum that is offered by sponsoring employers through cooperative agreements with the school.Optional Practical Training (OPT) is training that is not an integral part of a student’s established curriculum. OPT is not intended to fulfill the requirements of a student’s program of study and successful program completion does not require participation in OPT; it is optional. In contrast, CPT fulfills an integral element of an established curriculum and successful completion is contingent on participation in CPT.In any instance where an elective course is optional, making the CPT optional, the integral and required aspects of CPT would not be met. CPT is an integral part of an established curriculum and the practical training is required for all students participating in that curriculum, regardless of citizenship.Yes. Unlike OPT, participation in CPT is not optional for any student participating in an established curriculum that the school has determined requires CPT as an integral part of the educational experience. This means that all students — foreign and American — are required to participate in practical training if they are enrolled in an established curriculum where practical training is integral.The question-answer part of the memo said that while auditing and investigating schools to ensure compliance, SEVP (Student and Exchange Visitor Program) has noted that some institutions have described CPT as if it is optional practical training and not integral, despite clear regulatory requirements. SEVP has also discovered that some institutions have not required all students enrolled in the same established curriculum to participate in practical training, despite clear regulatory requirements that CPT is permitted only where the practical training is an integral part of an established curriculum.Yes. Foreign students must make an official request for authorization for CPT to their DSO so that the school can confirm that the student is participating in an established curriculum where practical training is integral, make a determination that the training is directly related to the student’s major area of study, and update the student’s SEVIS record to ensure that DHS can conduct proper oversight as required under federal law.Yes. Schools should only enter into cooperative agreements with legitimate, bona fide employers who are able to provide a quality practical training experience to students. CPT students should have access to practical training managed by an employer who has entered into a cooperative agreement with a school where it is agreed the employer will sponsor the school’s students for specific training such as an alternative work/study, internship, cooperative education or any other type of required internship or practicum that is specific to the student’s major area of study. Students are not expected to obtain EADs for this training which is an integral and required part of the curriculum.Immigration attorney Emily Neumann said this is not how CPT is used by universities. "When an agency needs a second, three-page broadcast just 12 days later to explain what the first one meant, that tells you the first one raised some serious questions," Neumann wrote.
Article Summary: Immigration and Customs Enforcement issued another memo clarifying and doubling down on the new restrictions. Many universities, including UC Berkeley, UC Davis, UC San Diego, Purdue, Santa Clara paused the approvals of CPT programs. CPT allows F-1 students to gain off-campus work experience, internships, before graduating.

Article Title: In 1903, rabbits were released on Hawaii’s Laysan Island as a food source; within a decade they had nearly stripped it bare, and three of its five landbird species eventually went extinct
Article Text:
Laysan Island's ecosystem was devastated after rabbits introduced in 1903 stripped away native vegetation

Devastating losses among native birds

Narrow escape for surviving species

Eradication and recovery

When German immigrant Max Schlemmer brought a small number of domestic rabbits to the isolated Pacific atoll of Laysan in 1903, he hoped to create a profitable meat-canning business. He also saw the animals as a source of entertainment for his children while he worked on guano extraction operations. Instead, the decision caused one of the worst ecological disasters in modern conservation history. Within a decade, the rabbits had stripped much of the island of its vegetation and eventually helped drive three of its five unique landbird species to extinction. Historical records preserved by the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument show how quickly the rabbit population grew across the isolated 1,000-acre atoll. With no natural predators and an enormous appetite, the rabbits consumed vegetation faster than the island could replace it. Over the next 20 years, the uncontrolled population destroyed 26 native plant species, including the unique Laysan fan palm (Pritchardia) and native sandalwood trees (Santalum ellipticum). A once-green habitat for birds was gradually turned into a landscape of bare sand.The destruction of the island's vegetation had a severe effect on its native birds.Before non-native mammals arrived, Laysan supported huge seabird colonies and five species of landbirds that existed nowhere else in the world. As shrubs, tussock grass and trees disappeared, so did insects and places where birds could shelter and nest. The loss of vegetation contributed to the extinction of three endemic birds: the Laysan millerbird (Acrocephalus familiaris familiaris), Laysan rail (Zapornia palmeri) and Laysan honeycreeper (Himatione fraithii). Scientific records from the 1923 Tanager Expedition documented the final days of the Laysan honeycreeper. The expedition was organised by the US Department of Agriculture's Bureau of Biological Survey and the Bernice P. Bishop Museum. Ornithologist Alexander Wetmore recorded that the last three Laysan honeycreepers died during a severe sandstorm while scientists were on the island trying to remove the remaining rabbits. The small, flightless Laysan rail survived for a time on nearby Midway Atoll after birds were introduced there in 1891. However, that population was later wiped out during World War II after rats were accidentally introduced to the atoll. This resulted in the complete extinction of the species.Only two of Laysan's endemic landbirds survived the crisis: the Laysan finch (Telespiza cantans) and the critically endangered Laysan duck (Anas laysanensis). Both species survived partly by changing what they ate. They began feeding on carrion, abandoned seabird eggs and brine flies around the island's central hypersaline lagoon. According to a historical overview and restoration plan from the US Fish and Wildlife Service, the Laysan duck population fell to dangerously low levels during the habitat destruction. By the early 20th century, fewer than 20 birds were believed to remain in the world. As the damage spread across the Northwestern Hawaiian Archipelago, President Theodore Roosevelt took action. In 1909, he issued an executive order creating the Hawaiian Islands Bird Reservation. Federal authorities later removed Schlemmer from Laysan following indictments linked to illegal feather collection and the unauthorised introduction of invasive species.By 1918, the rabbits had consumed much of their own food supply. Only a few hundred starving animals remained on an island with badly damaged vegetation. The crisis finally ended in 1923, when the Tanager Expedition arrived on Laysan with armed field crews tasked with finding and killing the remaining rabbits. After the rabbits were completely removed, the US Fish and Wildlife Service began long-term habitat restoration work. Conservation efforts continue today under the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument. Over the following decades, native bunchgrass (Eragrostis variabilis) and coastal shrubs slowly returned. Their growth helped stabilise the soil and reduce the sandstorms that had threatened the island's central lagoon. Conservationists have also reintroduced related plant species and created protected populations of the surviving Laysan duck and Laysan finch on other protected atolls, including Midway and Eastern Island. To help replace an extinct bird, federal wildlife managers also moved the closely related Nihoa millerbird (Acrocephalus familiaris kingi) from Nihoa Island to Laysan in 2011. The new population became established successfully, marking an important step in rebuilding an island ecosystem that had been severely damaged by a small group of domestic rabbits introduced more than a century earlier.
Article Summary: German immigrant Max Schlemmer brought domestic rabbits to Laysan Island in 1903. The rabbits consumed vegetation faster than the island could replace it. The destruction of the island's vegetation had a severe effect on its native birds. The loss of vegetation contributed to the extinction of three endemic birds. Conservation efforts continue today under the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument.

Article Title: Thousands of dragonflies are suddenly swarming across California, and the insects could help farmers control crop pests naturally
Article Text:
Dragonfly in San Jose, California. Image Credit: Wikimedia Commons

Warm spring rains triggering huge dragonfly swarms

Rhionaeschna californica found in Refuge Wildlife Viewing Area, first darner to be seen in spring. Image Credit: Bob Danley / USFWS

What dragonflies are doing around farms in California

Why are dragonflies such effective hunters

Beaverpond clubtail. Image Credit: Reuven Martin/Wikipedia

Life cycle of dragonflies

California is seeing an unusual surge in dragonflies, with large groups appearing over parks, ponds and farms after warm spring and early summer rain. The insects have been especially noticeable around the San Francisco Bay Area, where residents have reported seeing dozens flying together. Oakland nursery owner Peter Veilleux even counted about 100 dragonflies in one group while walking his dog near Lake Merritt. The sudden appearance may look mysterious, but experts say weather conditions probably created the right opportunity for the insects to spread. According to The Associated Press(AP), dragonfly expert Kathy Biggs believes warm monsoon storms helped drive the increase, with many of the insects likely being ‘wandering gliders,’ a migratory species capable of travelling long distances. For Californians, the spectacle is not only striking but also useful, because these natural predators feed on mosquitoes and crop pests.Kathy Biggs, a dragonfly expert and co-author of ‘Dragonflies of California,’ told AP that unusually warm monsoon storms moved through the state during late spring and early summer. Those conditions appear to have helped produce the huge number now being seen. Many of the dragonflies are probably wandering gliders.Unlike species that remain close to the water where they emerge, wandering gliders are highly migratory and can turn up in large numbers when weather conditions are favourable. The insects can travel long distances by taking advantage of changes in air pressure. Biggs described their movement as effectively ‘surfing’ the pressure systems created by the monsoon weather. They can reach speeds of about 35 mph (56 kph), allowing them to cover considerable distances. That explains why people in different parts of California can suddenly encounter large swarms of dragonflies. The insects do not necessarily remain in one location for long. Biggs said migratory species can stay somewhere for only a few days before moving on.The swarms are more than an unusual summer sight. They are also providing farmers with a natural form of pest control. AP reported that Joe Del Bosque, who farms in Fresno County noticed unusually large numbers of dragonflies flying about 10 to 20 feet (3 to 6 metres) above him earlier in August. Dragonflies are welcome visitors on his farm because they prey on insects that can damage crops. Del Bosque said the dragonflies feed on aphids, whiteflies and fruit flies, while also catching larger flying insects such as adult aphids and moths. He compared the insects to tiny fighter jets because of the way they rapidly chase and capture prey in mid-air. Ladybirds also help control pests around the crops, but dragonflies bring a different advantage by targeting insects while they are flying.Dragonflies are remarkably efficient predators. Chris Grinter, senior collection manager of entomology at the California Academy of Sciences in San Francisco, said that their strong flight muscles, excellent vision and agility make them particularly effective hunters. More than 90% of their hunting attempts are successful. He also said a dragonfly can eat hundreds of mosquitoes in a single day. That makes the sudden California swarms potentially beneficial for people as well as farms. California has about 70 species of dragonflies, although most are not migratory. Many remain close to the places where they emerge. The wandering gliders responsible for much of the current spectacle are different because they can travel with changing weather systems.The swarms seen above California are only the brief flying stage of a much longer life cycle. Dragonflies spend most of their lives underwater. After mating, females lay tiny eggs in freshwater. Once the eggs hatch, the young insects, known as nymphs, remain underwater and hunt other small creatures. According to AP, this underwater stage can last at least six months and, for some species, as long as five years. During that time, nymphs can feed on mosquito larvae, tadpoles and even other dragonfly nymphs. Eventually, they emerge from the water, shed their skin and become the familiar four-winged insects seen around ponds and fields. Their wings can move independently, allowing them to fly forwards, backwards, upwards and downwards and even hover in place. Once airborne, however, their lives are relatively short. Adults may survive for only a few weeks or months, spending that time hunting, moving between freshwater habitats and reproducing.People who enjoy watching dragonflies can make their gardens more welcoming to them. Biggs recommends avoiding pesticides and creating fish-free ponds where dragonflies can reproduce. Sunny areas with places for the insects to perch can also provide suitable conditions. Such spaces can offer dragonflies somewhere to rest while giving them access to the small insects they hunt. The sight nevertheless offers a reminder of how quickly insects can respond when weather, water and food come together.
Article Summary: California is seeing an unusual surge in dragonflies, with large groups appearing over parks, ponds and farms after warm spring and early summer rain. The insects have been especially noticeable around the San Francisco Bay Area, where residents have reported seeing dozens flying together. Experts believe warm monsoon storms helped drive the increase, with many of the insects likely being ‘wandering gliders,’ a migratory species capable of travelling long distances.

Article Title: New Mexico has protected nearly 11,000 acres along the Mimbres River as a new wildlife area, safeguarding historic water rights, rare river habitat and a 2-mile stretch of the desert stream
Article Text:
An elevated, high-definition view of the newly protected landscape surrounding the Mimbres River in southwestern New Mexico.

Protecting water rights and desert habitat

Protecting rare fish and wildlife

Broad support for the project

Conservationists and state officials in New Mexico have completed a deal to buy nearly 11,000 acres of ecologically rich land along the Mimbres River, permanently protecting an important desert watershed and creating the state's newest public conservation preserve. The purchase secures the newly created Mimbres Ranch Wildlife Management Area (WMA), a large property bordering the Gila National Forest in southwestern New Mexico. The project was completed with help from the national non-profit Trust for Public Land (TPL) and the state government. The acquisition places about two miles of the Mimbres River under public ownership while protecting historic water rights that date back more than a century. The property also creates a large, connected area for native wildlife and expands public access along the scenic Trail of the Mountain Spirits Byway.A key part of the deal is the permanent protection of important pre-1907 water rights connected to the Mimbres River. In the dry American Southwest, these water rights have major legal and environmental importance. They were established before New Mexico adopted its wider water code and have senior priority under state law.Protecting the rights will help keep water flowing through the river rather than being diverted for industrial or large-scale municipal use. This will support the river's surrounding riparian bosque, a green area of trees and plants that depends on the water. The Mimbres River is part of a rare closed-basin desert stream system. Its water stays within the basin instead of flowing into an ocean or another major river system. This unusual system has created a unique habitat for plants and animals adapted to the valley."At a time when public lands are under threat across the country, New Mexico is leaning in on conservation," said Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham in an official release published by the State of New Mexico Newsroom. "Protecting nearly 11,000 acres along the Mimbres River means healthier wildlife, cleaner water, and more places for New Mexico families to hunt, fish, and get outside. New Mexicans will benefit from this investment for generations to come. "The new wildlife management area contains a mix of Southwestern habitats, including high-desert grasslands, pinyon-juniper woodlands, cottonwood forests along the river and areas of ponderosa pine. These habitats support large animals such as Rocky Mountain elk, mule deer, black bears and mountain lions. They also provide habitat for birds including Merriam's turkey and quail. The property also contains designated critical habitat for federally protected species, including the western yellow-billed cuckoo and Chiricahua leopard frog. State fisheries biologists said the property is also important for protecting native fish found in the Mimbres drainage."This will create additional habitat for conserving the Rio Grande sucker and Chihuahua chub," said Kirk Patten, Chief of the Fisheries Management Division at the New Mexico Department of Game and Fish, in coverage reported by Organ Mountain News. "Both these fish are native to the Mimbres drainage, and this acquisition will ensure they continue to thrive there for years to come." The WMA will also connect with the Gila National Forest and existing protected areas, including The Nature Conservancy's Mimbres River Preserve. This will join previously separated habitats into a larger, more connected landscape.The project received funding and legislative support through state conservation programmes, with environmental groups providing technical help. Representative Nathan Small, a Democrat from Las Cruces who supported funding for the project in the state legislature, highlighted the importance of the river and surrounding land. "Here in New Mexico, our land and water are sacred. The Mimbres River and its surrounding uplands vibrate with life, supporting hundreds of plant, animal, bird, and even rare fish species," Small stated in the official announcement published by Trust for Public Land. "The Mimbres Ranch WMA will enhance this ecosystem and create new recreation opportunities, including opportunities for New Mexico resident hunters." The property is also important for its history. It was once home to the ancient Mimbres culture, part of the Mogollon tradition and known for its distinctive black-on-white pottery made between about 1000 AD and 1150 AD.Jim Petterson, Mountain West Region Vice-President for the Trust for Public Land, said the purchase was the result of several years of cooperation between different groups. "This project represents a major win for wildlife, water and communities across New Mexico," said Petterson in an official press release. "By protecting this ecologically rich property, we are ensuring that this extraordinary landscape, home to rare species and critical waterways, will remain intact and accessible to the public for generations to come. "State officials also described the acquisition as a long-term investment in conservation, tourism and outdoor recreation. "This acquisition represents an investment in the long-term sustainability of New Mexico's treasured wildlife, as well as its outdoor heritage," said Mike Sloane, Director of the New Mexico Department of Game and Fish, in statements carried by the Governor's Office. "Protecting this landscape helps conserve habitat for big game, native fish and other species, while creating new opportunities for the public to enjoy our state's outdoor spaces. "Located near both the Gila Wilderness and the Aldo Leopold Wilderness, the Mimbres Ranch Wildlife Management Area is expected to eventually offer hiking, licensed seasonal hunting, horseback riding and bird watching. The New Mexico Department of Game and Fish said detailed management plans and rules for public access will be released after initial assessments of the property are completed.
Article Summary: Conservationists and state officials in New Mexico have completed a deal to buy nearly 11,000 acres of ecologically rich land along the Mimbres River. The acquisition places about two miles of the river under public ownership while protecting historic water rights that date back more than a century. The property also creates a large, connected area for native wildlife and expands public access.

Article Title: Five labourers gunned down at construction site in Pakistan's Balochistan
Article Text: Five labourers from Pakistan’s Punjab province were shot dead at a construction site in Balochistan’s Pishin district, a provincial government official said Tuesday, according to news agency PTI.The labourers were killed by unidentified gunmen in Saranan town on Monday morning, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said. Their bodies were sent to their hometowns in Punjab for burial.Arrangements were made to transport the bodies to their respective villages in Ahmedpur Sharqia and Bahawalpur, Rind said. Security forces have launched a search operation to track down the attackers.Balochistan chief minister Sarfaraz Bugti condemned the killings and vowed action against those responsible."Those shedding the blood of innocent laborers deserve no leniency," Bugti said in a statement issued by his office. "The cowardly acts of terrorists cannot weaken the provincial government's resolve."Saranan town has witnessed militant attacks since last week. A few days ago, gunmen attacked a police station in the town and fled with weapons, ammunition and two vehicles.Banned Baloch insurgent groups have frequently targeted workers and labourers from other provinces working in Balochistan.In July, five barbers from Multan were shot dead in Mashkail town after armed men on motorcycles opened fire at their barber shop.Last month, six labourers from Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa were abducted in the Nasirabad area of Turbat district. Their bullet-riddled bodies were later found in a remote area, police said.Security and law enforcement agencies have been conducting a large-scale operation against insurgent groups in parts of Balochistan since early July. However, the attacks have continued.In a separate incident on Sunday, five policemen were injured when two unidentified men hurled a hand grenade at a police post in Ambar tehsil of Mohmand district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.Police retaliated with gunfire, forcing the attackers to flee. The injured policemen were taken to a nearby hospital and are said to be out of danger. An investigation is underway.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which borders Afghanistan, has witnessed recurring militant violence, including attacks linked to insurgent groups, cross-border movement of fighters and repeated military operations.
Article Summary: The labourers were killed by unidentified gunmen in Saranan town on Monday morning. Security forces have launched a search operation to track down the attackers. Baloch insurgent groups have frequently targeted workers and labourers from other provinces working in Balochistan. In July, five barbers from Multan were shot dead in Mashkail town.

Article Title: Pakistan army officer pulls gun, fires in air amid student protest at Peshawar university- video
Article Text:
Sarhad University, Peshawar, Pakistan (Picture from X)

A Pakistan army officer opened fire into the air during a student protest at Sarhad University in Peshawar, triggering chaos and a scuffle on the campus, according to local media reports and videos circulating online.The incident comes amid growing unrest in Pakistan, with protests and demonstrations also being reported from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Balochistan, adding to the challenges facing the country's military and political establishment.According to reports, the officer, said to be a colonel, was the husband of a faculty member at Sarhad University. He reportedly got into a heated confrontation with protesting students, which soon escalated into a physical scuffle.Videos shared by several social media accounts purportedly show the officer striking students with a stick amid the confrontation. As tensions escalated, he allegedly pulled out a pistol and initially pointed it towards the protesters before raising the weapon in the air.The officer was then seen firing shots into the air, sparking panic and further uproar on the university campus.Reports said the officer has been taken into custody, while the Pakistan army has ordered an inquiry into the incident.
Article Summary: Pakistan army officer opened fire during student protest at Sarhad University. Incident triggered chaos and a scuffle on the campus, according to reports. Incident comes amid growing unrest in Pakistan, with protests and demonstrations also being reported from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Balochistan.

Article Title: ‘CTA intentionally prevented’: PTI alleges negligence over Imran Khan’s hospital visit
Article Text:
Imran Khan’s medical care under scrutiny

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the inquiry committee established by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will lead to accountability? Yes, it will No, it won't 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of former Prime Minister Imran Khan, on Monday criticised what it called the “continued failure” of authorities at a state-run hospital, alleging that a CT Coronary Angiography (CTA) scheduled for Khan was not conducted despite cardiologists warning of potential cardiac complications.In a statement on Sunday, PTI central secretary Information Sheikh Waqas Akram said authorities had failed to provide the 73-year-old Khan with the medically recommended diagnostic test despite a functional CT scanner being available at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), Dawn reported."This cannot be dismissed as an isolated administrative lapse; it reflects a deeply troubling pattern,” Akram said.Akram also cited a Supreme Court order directing Khan to undergo a comprehensive medical examination and treatment at Shifa International Hospital.He alleged that authorities had bypassed the directive and instead transferred Khan to a facility where the CT angiography was not conducted.“When the necessary facilities were available at Shifa International, deliberately taking Khan to a hospital unable or unwilling to perform the procedure raises a grave question: was the decision made in advance to prevent the CT Coronary Angiography from being conducted?” he asked."Even the government’s own doctors considered this diagnostic test necessary,” Akram added.Akram said a government medical board examined Khan on August 10 after he complained of heart palpitations and severe headaches.He said a cardiologist at PIMS had recommended a CTA on August 1 after Khan experienced fluctuating blood pressure and restlessness, citing potential cardiac complications given his age and prolonged isolation.Taking note of the reports, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday formed an inquiry committee, headed by the Establishment Division secretary, to establish the facts and determine responsibility.Commenting on the Prime Minister’s decision to constitute an inquiry committee following reports that Imran Khan’s CTA was not conducted, Akram said the move raised “serious questions as to why the medically recommended test was not conducted in the first instance. Why coordination between the cardiology and radiology departments had failed, and why Imran Khan was not taken to Shifa International despite the availability of the required facilities there”."Imran Khan’s heart health cannot be subjected to political calculations, administrative excuses or further delay,” Akram said."Political victimisation must never be permitted to endanger a human life through the denial or postponement of essential medical care. The decision to take him to a facility where the required test was not conducted, despite the availability of the necessary facilities at Shifa International, has created serious concerns that the procedure was intentionally prevented,” he alleged."The government and all relevant authorities will bear full responsibility for any further deterioration in his condition,” Akram added.Meanwhile, former India captains Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar are among 21 former international cricket captains who have written to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, urging authorities to ensure proper medical treatment and the welfare of Imran Khan.The letter, initiated by former Australia captain Greg Chappell, marks the second appeal by former international cricketers calling for humane treatment and adequate medical care for the 73-year-old Khan.Khan was arrested on August 5, 2023, in connection with a corruption case and has remained in custody since then. He is currently lodged in Adiala Jail, a detention facility on the outskirts of Rawalpindi.Khan’s relatives and supporters have repeatedly alleged human rights violations and accused authorities of restricting his access to adequate medical care, family visits and legal counsel.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of former Prime Minister Imran Khan, on Monday criticised what it called the “continued failure” of authorities at a state-run hospital. PTI alleges that a CT Coronary Angiography (CTA) scheduled for Khan was not conducted despite cardiologists warning of potential cardiac complications. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday formed an inquiry committee, headed by the Establishment Division secretary.

Article Title: ‘You are powerful, but remember 1971?’ Pakistani politician takes fresh swipe at Army
Article Text:
Fazlur Rehman (File photo)

(With ANI inputs)

Pakistani politician and Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman continued his verbal attacks on the Pakistan Army, recalling the military's decisive defeat in the 1971 war with India that led to the creation of Bangladesh, then known as East Pakistan.“‘We are the protectors of this country. No one’s father can harm this country.’ I agree, you are very powerful,” Rehman remarked at a JUI (F) convention in Peshawar, targeting Pakistan’s top military leadership.He recalled how the Pakistan Army laid down its arms in 1971, just a day after then-President and military ruler General Yahya Khan declared that it would fight until the end."But I remember, and maybe there are some elders who remember, that in December 1971, one day before laying down arms, General Yahya Khan addressed the army and said, we will fight in the streets, in the deserts, in the fields, in the factories, in the mountains, and we will fight against them. We will fight. We heard these big words then," Rehman added.The JUI-F further chief questioned why the public is being subjected to "severe hardships" while the establishment remains "insensitive" to their misery.“Why are you putting the country and the people to the test? Why are you having fun when your public is suffering? And today is 2026. When the revolution came in Afghanistan in 1989, and the war started, now you tell me, it’s been 45-46 years, blood has been flowing on the same line for about half a century.When blood flows like this, then it is a sign of geographical changes,” Rehman remarked.Warning that persistent state oppression and ongoing conflict threaten the nation’s integrity and could signal territorial disintegration, he stated, “It is a sign of oppression. Then at least inform us of your intentions. We are tolerating it and will continue to tolerate it. It will continue. A few more days, my dear, just a few more days. We are forced to take a breath in the shade of oppression. If we endure the oppression for a little longer, if we suffer, if we cry, it is the legacy of our ancestors. We are helpless.”Rehman’s remarks came days after he challenged the military to enter politics directly, declaring, “If you want to do politics, then take off the uniform and come; participate in the elections, and it will become clear what votes people give to those in uniform. It is your prerogative to give government to whomever you want, and to snatch it away from whomever you wish.”
Article Summary: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman continued his verbal attacks on the Pakistan Army. He recalled the military's decisive defeat in the 1971 war with India that led to the creation of Bangladesh. He questioned why the public is being subjected to "severe hardships" while the establishment remains "insensitive"

Article Title: Pakistan: Security official killed by unidentified gunmen; 5 cops injured in separate grenade blast
Article Text:
According to police, two unidentified armed men targeted the security official. (Photo credit: IANS)

Five policemen injured in grenade attack

A security official was killed on Sunday after unidentified gunmen opened fire in northwest Pakistan, police said, according to news agency PTI.The incident took place within the jurisdiction of Badaber Police Station on the outskirts of Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.According to police, two unidentified armed men riding a motorcycle targeted the official, who was posted with the Counter Terrorism Department.He was killed on the spot, while the assailants fled the scene following the attack. Police cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to trace the attackers.No individual or group has so far claimed responsibility for the attack.In a separate incident in Mohmand district, five policemen were injured when two unidentified men hurled a hand grenade at a police post in Ambar tehsil, police said.Police retaliated with gunfire, forcing the attackers to flee. The injured policemen were taken to a nearby hospital and are said to be out of danger. An investigation is underway.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which borders Afghanistan, has witnessed recurring militant violence, cross-border movement of fighters and military operations.Pakistan's federal government has blamed the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) for attacks in areas bordering Afghanistan since a ceasefire agreement between the two sides ended in November 2022.
Article Summary: A security official was killed on Sunday after unidentified gunmen opened fire in northwest Pakistan. In a separate incident, five policemen were injured when two unidentified men hurled a hand grenade at a police post in Ambar tehsil. The injured policemen were taken to a nearby hospital and are said to be out of danger.

Article Title: Pakistan power crisis: Karachi residents riot amid outages lasting hours, block major roads
Article Text:
Protesters blocked major roads and intersections, burned tyres and clashed with K-Electric personnel over prolonged blackouts (ANI photo)

Power protests erupted across several parts of Karachi as residents took to the streets over prolonged and unannounced outages, blocking major roads and burning tyres while demanding restoration of electricity.Demonstrations were reported in Pak Colony, Liaquatabad, Gharibabad, Nishtar Road, Bhimpura and Ranchore Line, disrupting traffic across key parts of Pakistan’s commercial capital. In Liaquatabad, protesters blocked major intersections, while clashes between traders and K-Electric (KE) staff over outages escalated into tyre-burning on Nishtar Road, as reported by local news outle Dawn.Residents said they were facing 12 hours or more of daily power cuts, often without adequate notice. The outages have also disrupted water supplies as pumping stations remain shut when electricity is unavailable, adding to public anger.“Bill-paying citizens are being punished with 12-hour load-shedding,” a protester in Liaquatabad said.The crisis also hit businesses and households, with residents reporting spoiled food, disrupted studies and sleepless nights as fans remained unusable during blackouts.The protests compounded an already severe traffic situation in the city. Roads were also closed for traditional Chup Tazia processions, while the power protests triggered additional blockades. Traffic police diverted vehicles to alternative routes, but those too became congested.Asif Khan, a private-sector employee, told Dawn he took four hours to travel from SITE to Liaquatabad after leaving work around 5pm. Another commuter said an ambulance carrying his feverish mother was stuck for about two hours near Civic Centre while they were travelling to a doctor in Saddar.“We pay bills on time but still face 12-hour power outages. Today we couldn’t even reach home,” commuter Imran from Gharibabad said.KE, however, attributed the prolonged outages in some affected areas to electricity theft and unpaid bills. A company spokesperson said outstanding dues from defaulters in Bandhani Colony and Rexer Line had crossed PKR 3 billion, adding that the duration of load-shedding depended on “electricity theft and the level of losses in the area”.The protests come as Karachi continues to grapple with an electricity crisis that is also affecting water supply, businesses and daily life across densely populated neighbourhoods.
Article Summary: Demonstrations reported in Pak Colony, Liaquatabad, Gharibabad, Nishtar Road, Bhimpura and Ranchore Line. Protesters blocked major roads and intersections, burned tyres and clashed with K-Electric personnel. Residents said they were facing 12 hours or more of daily power cuts, often without adequate notice.

Article Title: 'India could use water as weapon': Pakistan minister as Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance
Article Text:
Pakistan minister Ahsan Iqbal (File photo)

Pakistan minister Ahsan Iqbal has said India could “weaponise” the Indus Water Treaty (IWT) and expressed hope that “better sense” would prevail to prevent the two neighbours from going to war again, this time over water.He noted that the treaty had remained “untouchable” for almost seven decades since it was signed in 1960, but New Delhi has now been kept in abeyance “unilaterally."“...Indus Water Treaty that has stood the test of time for the last 70 years. India and Pakistan fought several wars, but it (IWT) was considered untouchable because it is an international agreement, and this time around the Indian government has unilaterally held it in abeyance... first time probably water has been weaponised in history,” Iqbal told the Asia Society.“We (Pakistan) now face this threat that they (India) can use water as a weapon to deny Pakistan when it needs it for its crops and release it when we don't need it... We are using all the diplomatic means to make sure that we don't have future wars on water because we have already seen lots of wars,” the minister added.He further stated that South Asian countries should instead focus on issues such as development, poverty, illiteracy and the youth “bulge”, describing the region as the “least integrated” in the world."So we hope that there is better sense in our neighbour's (India) mind and we don't see that water is weaponised and we go to another conflict with India over water because Pakistan cannot surrender at any cost the future of its 250 million people for its food security and right of water. If we let it happen, then every state that is on the lower side of water supply would be hostage to any country that controls the rivers," the Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz) leader remarked.Iqbal's remarks came days after Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif warned India of a “direct response” for putting the IWT in abeyance.“India proved itself an enemy of peace by unilaterally and illegally suspending the Indus Waters Treaty. I declare in clear terms that every single drop of Pakistan's water is our red line. If India does not come to its senses, it will be responded to directly,” Sharif said on August 13, on the eve of Pakistan's Independence Day.New Delhi put the agreement in abeyance following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year. Since then, Pakistani leaders have repeatedly called water their “red line” and threatened India over the move, describing it as an “act of war.”
Article Summary: Ahsan Iqbal says India could use water as a weapon to deny Pakistan when it needs it for its crops. New Delhi put the agreement in abeyance following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year. Pakistani leaders have repeatedly called water their “red line” and threatened India.

Article Title: ‘In contempt for gathering people’: Pak blames ex PM Imran Khan’s party for hospital transfer
Article Text:
Pakistan government statement on Imran Khan's hospital transfer

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you view the involvement of PTI workers during Imran Khan transfer to the hospital? Justified, they were supporting their leader Unsure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Govt says court order was followed

NEW DELHI: The Pakistan government on Saturday blamed jailed former prime minister Imran Khan ’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party for his transfer to a state-run hospital instead of the private facility ordered by the Supreme Court for his medical checkup.Information minister Attaullah Tarar said the government was forced to take 73-year-old Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) after a large number of PTI workers gathered outside Shifa International Hospital.The development came after Khan’s sister, Uzma Khan, approached the Supreme Court alleging that the government and senior officials had violated its order to shift the former prime minister to the private hospital.The Supreme Court had on August 18 directed authorities to transfer Khan from Adiala jail to Shifa Hospital within two days and keep him there until the next hearing on September 16. Instead, Khan was taken to PIMS and later returned to jail after doctors declared him fit.Tarar alleged that PTI workers gathered along the route to Shifa Hospital, removed barriers and created social media content, leaving authorities with no option but to shift Khan elsewhere.“Contempt has definitely happened,” Tarar said, accusing Khan’s sister and PTI of violating the court’s directions by turning the medical checkup into a political issue.The minister maintained that the government had implemented the Supreme Court’s order “in letter and spirit”. He said the medical examination was conducted transparently, Khan’s sister was present and doctors from Shifa Hospital were involved in the process.The Supreme Court’s order followed months of concerns raised by Khan’s family and supporters over his health, particularly an eye condition diagnosed earlier this year. Khan was taken to PIMS several times after being diagnosed with right central retinal vein occlusion in late January.A report submitted by jail authorities to the Supreme Court said his eye condition had improved significantly and that his vision was “almost normal”.Khan has been lodged in Rawalpindi’s Adiala Jail since 2023 in connection with several cases.
Article Summary: Pakistan government blames jailed former prime minister Imran Khan ’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party for his transfer to a state-run hospital. Information minister Attaullah Tarar said the government was forced to take 73-year-old Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences. Tarar alleged that PTI workers gathered along the route to Shifa Hospital, removed barriers and created social media content.

Article Title: Big crisis brewing in Rawalpindi? Pakistan deploys army for ‘sensitive duties’
Article Text:
The decision comes days after a man allegedly linked to former prime minister Imran Khan's party.

Army deployment follows security incident

Rawalpindi has strategic importance

The Pakistan government has authorised the deployment of the army in Rawalpindi for six months following a request from the Punjab home department for what it described as "sensitive security duties".The decision allows three companies of the Pakistan Army to be deployed in the city under Article 245 of the Pakistani Constitution, which permits the armed forces to assist the civil administration in maintaining security."The federal government, exercising the powers conferred under Article 245 of the Constitution of Pakistan, is pleased to authorise the deployment of three companies of the Pakistan Army for sensitive security duties in Rawalpindi," according to a notification issued by the Ministry of Interior and Narcotics Control on Friday.The notification said the deployment was intended to prevent a potential security problem and ensure that authorities could respond quickly if an unexpected situation arose.It said that the decision was taken "to avoid any undesirable situation as well as to respond effectively in any unforeseen situation as per the requirement of the district administration".The decision comes days after a man allegedly linked to former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party opened fire at security forces in Rawalpindi.He was subsequently killed in retaliatory firing.State-run PTV News, citing security sources, reported that the attacker was a resident of Khyber district and an "active PTI member". According to the report, a PTI flag, bullets and weapons were recovered from him.The PTI, however, rejected any connection with the incident. The party said it had nothing to do with terrorism and accused authorities of attempting to associate the party with the attack.The deployment is particularly significant because Rawalpindi is home to the Pakistan Army's General Headquarters, the military's top command centre.The city is therefore an important military and administrative centre, and the decision to deploy army personnel there comes amid heightened security concerns following the recent shooting incident.The deployment has been authorised for six months, with the troops to perform duties requested by the district administration under the constitutional provision allowing the military to assist civilian authorities.
Article Summary: Three companies of the Pakistan Army will be deployed in Rawalpindi for six months. The decision comes after a man allegedly linked to Imran Khan's party opened fire in the city. The deployment is intended to prevent a potential security problem and ensure that authorities can respond quickly.

Article Title: 'Repeatedly tortured': Imran Khan's sister alleges abuse in jail as ex-Pakistan PM returns to prison
Article Text:
‘He was repeatedly tortured in jail’: Imran Khan's sister alleges mistreatment

PTI files contempt petition

Supporters gather after brief hospital visit

Pakistan's jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan repeatedly told his sister that he was being tortured in prison, she said on Saturday, a day after he was taken to a state-run hospital for a brief medical examination and sent back to jail.Khan's sister, Uzma Khan, attended his examination at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad and said the former prime minister was physically fit but had repeatedly complained of torture.“Khan told me that he is being repeatedly tortured in prison”, she told the media.The interior and law ministries, along with jail authorities, have not responded to a Reuters request for comment on the allegation.Khan was taken to PIMS overnight on Friday after the Supreme Court had directed authorities to transfer him from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for a medical examination. He was declared medically fit and returned to prison within hours.Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party on Saturday filed a contempt petition against the government, accusing authorities of violating the Supreme Court's order by taking him to PIMS instead of the private hospital named by the court.The petition seeks action against senior government officials and asks that Khan be taken to Shifa International Hospital for treatment, PTI legal adviser Naeem Panjutha said."The petition seeks action against the ​prime minister, law minister, information minister" and other government officials, Panjutha said, adding that it also calls for Khan's treatment at the private hospital ordered by the court.The PTI also alleged that Khan was denied access to his personal physician, which it said amounted to another breach of the Supreme Court's directive.A three-judge Supreme Court bench had on Tuesday directed authorities to transfer Khan from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital within two days for a medical examination.The PTI interprets the order as requiring Khan to remain under medical supervision until at least mid-September.Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the decision to take Khan to PIMS instead of the court-named private hospital was made because of security concerns.Khan declared medically fit, sent back to jailKhan was examined by a team of doctors, including an ophthalmologist, cardiologist and physician, before being declared medically fit and sent back to Adiala jail in Rawalpindi."A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist and a physician conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit," Tarar said.Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and maintains that the cases against him are politically motivated. The government denies the allegation.His lawyers have previously said his health has deteriorated in prison and that he has suffered substantial loss of vision in his right eye. The government has maintained that medical reports have found no condition requiring immediate treatment.Khan's supporters gathered along roads in Islamabad overnight, throwing flowers at a vehicle believed to be carrying him to the hospital.The scenes were broadcast live on Pakistani television, in a notable departure from recent years when broadcasters often avoided mentioning Khan's name.PTI leaders have warned that the latest developments could increase pressure on the government and fuel fresh demonstrations."After what happened yesterday, the pressure (on authorities) will double," Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said, adding that preparations for a protest march planned for September 27 had picked up.Khan's arrest and imprisonment have remained a major source of political tension in Pakistan. His arrest in 2023 triggered widespread protests, including attacks on military installations, and his supporters continue to demand his release.
Article Summary: Imran Khan repeatedly told his sister that he was being tortured in prison, she says. Khan was taken to a state-run hospital for a brief medical examination and sent back to jail. He was declared medically fit and returned to prison within hours. Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and maintains that the cases against him are politically motivated.

Article Title: Imran Khan's kin say Pak govt violated court order for not taking ex-PM to private hospital
Article Text:
Imran Khan shifted back to jail after medical examination

Family alleges violation of court order

NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan was shifted back to Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi early Friday, hours after he was taken for a medical examination amid a legal battle over his health and demands from his family and supporters for better medical care.Khan, 73, was taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, Pakistan's information minister Attaullah Tarar said, news agaency PTI reports. The government later said Khan was medically fit and returned him to jail at around 5 am.The development came days after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move Khan to Al-Shifa hospital following a medical report that said he was suffering from “level three plus” anxiety.Khan's family has repeatedly raised concerns about his access to adequate medical treatment while in custody. His sister, Uzma Khan, was present during the medical examination at PIMS, according to AP. They have accused authorities of violating a court order by taking him to a government hospital for a medical examination instead of a private hospital designated by the court.She alleged that during their meeting, Khan complained of being kept in solitary confinement, which she described as “mental torture” for the former prime minister.Khan’s personal physician, Faisal Sultan, said he had been taken to Shifa International Hospital, where he waited for Khan until early Friday. He was later informed that Khan had instead been returned to Adiala prison in Rawalpindi.Tarar said authorities changed the plan because of security concerns after supporters of Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) gathered outside Shifa International Hospital or were heading there.Khan has been in custody since his arrest on August 5, 2023, in a corruption case.
Article Summary: Imran Khan, 73, was taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad. The government later said Khan was medically fit and returned him to jail at around 5 am. The development came days after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move Khan to Al-Shifa hospital.

Article Title: Ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan returns to Adiala Jail after medical examination at Islamabad hospital
Article Text:
73-year-old cricket legend facing health issues after 3 years of imprisonment

Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan on Friday returned to Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail shortly after undergoing a medical examination at Shifa Hospital in Islamabad.The development was confirmed to Reuters by a member of his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.The 73-year-old cricket legend has been facing health issues after spending more than three years in prison following his tenure as prime minister.Khan was taken to Shifa Hospital days after the Supreme Court ordered a medical examination. An official from the Shehbaz Sharif-led government said Islamabad was complying with the Supreme Court's order to facilitate his medical examination.Khan's party and family had sought permission for him to remain in hospital.A three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination amid prolonged concerns raised by his family and personal doctors over his health and access to treatment.The court directed that a medical board, including specialists and his personal physician, Faisal Sultan, examine him.The Supreme Court's order came after former Pakistan president Arif Alvi shared Khan's vitals and raised concerns over what he described as "alarming" medical reports.In a post on X, Alvi said, "Imran Khan's medical reports are alarming. I have gone through them with several specialists, and I am writing this in plain language so every Pakistani can understand exactly what is happening."Alvi also highlighted Khan's health concerns, citing his "anxiety and stress levels", "palpitations," and "high blood pressure." He added that while sleeplessness was not mentioned in the report, Khan's medication appeared to suggest the problem.
Article Summary: Imran Khan returned to Adiala Jail after medical examination at Shifa Hospital in Islamabad. Khan, 73, has been facing health issues after spending more than three years in prison following his tenure as prime minister. A three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination.

Article Title: Ex-Pak PM Imran Khan moved to private hospital from prison after SC order
Article Text:
Imran Khan’s transfer follows months of health concerns, including a dispute over worsening vision in his right eye

Imprisoned former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan was shifted from Adiala prison to a private hospital in Islamabad after midnight Thursday for a medical examination, news agency AP reported citing Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party's statement.Khan was taken to Shifa International Hospital hours after Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the government would comply with a Supreme Court order directing authorities to facilitate his medical examination.The PTI said the transfer was carried out following the Supreme Court's order earlier this week but did not provide further details. It remained unclear whether Khan would return to prison after the examination or stay at the hospital for further treatment. His family and party have sought permission for him to remain there.Earlier Thursday, Chaudhry said the government had approached the Supreme Court seeking clarification on whether the medical relief granted to Khan applied only to him or could also cover other prisoners. He stressed that the request was not aimed at delaying or defying the court's order.The three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination amid prolonged concerns raised by his family and personal doctors over his health and access to treatment.The court directed that a medical board examine him, including specialists and his personal physician, Faisal Sultan.The government has maintained that prisoners receive medical care under existing rules and can be moved to government hospitals when required.Concerns over Khan's health intensified in January after his family claimed he had lost about 85% of the vision in his right eye. The government disputed the claim and later said his vision had improved by around 70%.Khan, a former cricket star, was ousted as prime minister in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. He has remained imprisoned since 2023 after convictions in multiple cases, including a graft case.
Article Summary: Imran Khan was moved from Adiala prison to a private hospital in Islamabad after midnight Thursday for a medical examination. It remained unclear whether Khan would return to prison after the examination or stay at the hospital for further treatment. His family and party have sought permission for him to remain there. Khan, a former cricket star, was ousted as prime minister in a parliamentary no- confidence vote in April 2022.

Article Title: Red-faced Pakistan summons top diplomat over US envoy Gor's J&K remark in Srinagar
Article Text:
US Ambassador Sergio Gor visits Srinagar with J&K CM Omar

Pakistan on Wednesday summoned the top US diplomat Islamabad and lodged a protest after US envoy to India Sergio Gor described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India” during his visit to Srinagar on Wednesday.The remarks came as Gor made his first visit to Jammu and Kashmir since taking office and met chief minister Omar Abdullah.Gor’s comments were made during a joint media briefing with Abdullah following their meeting at the chief minister’s residence. “It’s a pleasure to be here. This is an important part of India. I am here, visiting for the first time. It is an incredibly beautiful place. I am thrilled to be here,” the US envoy said.Gor also indicated that Washington could reconsider its travel advisory for Jammu and Kashmir, saying the US regularly reviews its warnings. He said the Indian government and the Jammu and Kashmir administration had taken steps to improve safety in the region.“I cannot make any big announcements here today, but it is something we are going to look at,” Gor said, adding that the US would consider whether its existing travel warning should be downgraded.The ambassador also described his meeting with Abdullah as “very good” and said the two sides had discussed ways to deepen economic cooperation and create opportunities benefiting India and the US.Abdullah said the talks focused on what Washington could do for Jammu and Kashmir, while also referring to “certain legacy issues” that would need to be addressed.“We look forward to taking this conversation further,” Abdullah said, adding that he was “very hopeful and optimistic” that engagement between the US and Jammu and Kashmir would “both widen and deepen in the years ahead”.
Article Summary: Pakistan summons top US diplomat Islamabad and lodges a protest. US envoy to India Sergio Gor described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India’ Gor also indicated that Washington could reconsider its travel advisory for J&K.

Article Title: 3-yr-old’s rape-murder near Bihar border fuels death penalty debate in Nepal
Article Text:
The rape and murder of a three-year-old girl in Nepal sparked parliamentary demands for the death penalty

NEW DELHI: The rape and murder of a three-year-old girl in Nepal’s Bara district, around 25km from Raxaul in Bihar, triggered demands for the death penalty in parliament after days of protests, even as the principal suspect is a 16-year-old boy who, if convicted, would be sentenced under Nepal’s juvenile justice law. Lawmakers sought constitutional changes to allow capital punishment for heinous crimes, while RSP law minister Sobita Gautam and home minister Sudan Gurung told parliament that the govt could not introduce it without first amending the Constitution.The girl disappeared from Jeetpur-Simara on Aug 16 and her body was recovered two days later from an abandoned house near her home, leading to demonstrations in Simara, Kathmandu and other parts of Nepal. Police identified her teen neighbour as the principal suspect and widened the investigation, taking nine people into custody amid questions over whether officers had responded quickly enough after the family reported her missing.The killing dominated parliament proceedings, with ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) lawmaker Afsana Banu demanding an amendment to Article 16(2), which prohibits capital punishment, and calling for Nepal to reconsider its international commitments against the death penalty.“No international treaty or law can stand above citizens’ safety. Concern for the human rights of criminals cannot come at the cost of victims’ rights and justice,” she said, urging her govt to amend the Constitution to allow death penalty for heinous crimes.Other RSP lawmakers questioned whether the existing legal framework provided adequate punishment in such cases. Anushka Shrestha said, “A person should not escape severe punishment for a heinous crime merely because the perpetrator is a minor,” while arguing that punishment for rape needed review. Shraddha Kunwar raised a separate constitutional argument, asking whether parliament should focus only on the prohibition on death penalty or also ensure women’s constitutional right to live with dignity.Gautam, however, told parliament that Article 16(2) explicitly barred Nepal from making any law providing for capital punishment and pointed to the country's international human rights commitments. “No matter how intense public anger becomes, our govt cannot legislate beyond the Constitution,” she said. Nepal constitutionally abolished capital punishment in 1990 and retained the prohibition in its 2015 Constitution.The suspect’s age presents a separate legal issue even as lawmakers debate capital punishment. Under Nepal’s Children Act, 2018, anyone below 18 is dealt with under juvenile law, and an offender aged 16 to below 18 can receive two-thirds of the punishment prescribed for an adult. For adults, Nepal’s criminal law provides for imprisonment for the remainder of natural life for murder committed after rape, the maximum punishment available under the existing constitutional framework.Following days of protests, govt reached a three-point agreement with the victim’s family and formed a seven-member Garima Nyaya Sankalpa Samiti under law ministry, giving it seven days to recommend changes concerning sexual violence and offences against women and children.
Article Summary: The rape and murder of a three-year-old girl in Nepal sparked demands for the death penalty in parliament. Lawmakers sought constitutional changes to allow capital punishment for heinous crimes. The girl disappeared from Jeetpur-Simara on Aug 16 and her body was recovered two days later from an abandoned house near her home.

Article Title: Balen gets medical pass to wear trademark dark glasses in parliament
Article Text:
Nepal PM Balen Shah with home minister Sudan Gurung (right) and physical infrastructure minister Sunil Lamsal in a photograph Shah posted on social media earlier this year

Nepal parliament secretariat cleared PM Balendra Shah to wear his trademark dark sunglasses inside parliament on medical grounds after his office submitted a medical report, ending a row over whether such eyewear belonged in the House. Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal had earlier advised lawmakers against wearing dark glasses in the chamber following public criticism.Parliament secretariat spokesperson Ekaram Giri said Shah’s office submitted documents showing he needed them for medical reasons -- his doctor advised him to wear the shades because he had "discomfort seeing in bright light". Shah is scheduled to face lawmakers in a direct question-and-answer session on Wednesday, amid opposition criticism over his repeated absence from parliament.Shah’s rectangular black shades had long been part of his public image, accompanying the former rapper and Kathmandu mayor through his rise to Nepal’s top office. Ahead of Nepal’s March 5 elections, supporters dubbed the look “Balen dai ko chashma”, triggering a fashion craze among young voters. Similar black rectangular frames sold out at several Kathmandu shops and online stores as demand surged, with retailers marketing lookalikes. Often paired with his all-black outfits, the shades became one of the most recognisable symbols of Shah’s youth appeal.
Article Summary: Nepal parliament secretariat cleared PM Balendra Shah to wear his trademark dark sunglasses inside parliament on medical grounds. Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal had earlier advised lawmakers against wearing dark glasses in the chamber following public criticism. Shah is scheduled to face lawmakers in a direct question-and- answer session on Wednesday.

Article Title: 'Myanmar's human rights crisis has hit new low': UN flags atrocities against Rohingya
Article Text:
The human rights situation in Myanmar has reached a new low

Rohingya caught between two armed forces

Myanmar’s hidden mining economy

The human rights situation in Myanmar has reached a new low, with widespread atrocities against the Rohingya minority and a rapidly expanding illicit economy further deepening the suffering of civilians, the United Nations said on Tuesday.According to a report by the UN human rights office covering the period from June 2025 to May 2026, unrelenting conflict, military violence and a growing “conflict economy” have exposed millions of civilians to severe hardship.Both the Myanmar military and the Arakan Army, which controls large parts of Rakhine State, have been accused of systemic abuses against Rohingya communities. These include killings, torture, forced labour, forced recruitment, arbitrary detention, sexual violence and forced displacement.Nearly nine years after the military crackdown that triggered the mass exodus of Rohingya in 2017, the community continues to face persecution and displacement. The situation has deteriorated further since the military coup in February 2021 that ousted Aung San Suu Kyi and plunged the country into a prolonged civil war.The military-backed electoral process held earlier this year paved the way for junta leader Min Aung Hlaing to become president, while the military continued to consolidate its grip over the country.The UN said the military had continued to use airstrikes, arson and restrictions on humanitarian assistance to terrorise civilians and maintain control. At least 8,075 civilians, including 1,774 women and 1,074 children, have been killed since the 2021 coup, according to UN figures. The actual toll is believed to be significantly higher.Myanmar’s military has denied deliberately targeting civilians, saying its airstrikes were limited to military targets and were carried out in response to armed groups seizing towns and villages. It has also described several of the groups fighting it as terrorist organisations.The conflict has also triggered a massive humanitarian crisis. The number of internally displaced people has risen to about 3.6 million, while an estimated 12.4 million people are facing acute food insecurity. Among those affected are hundreds of thousands of women and children suffering from acute malnutrition.The UN has accused the Arakan Army of carrying out serious abuses against Rohingya communities in northern Rakhine, including arbitrary arrests, torture, sexual abuse and forced labour.The group has also been accused of seizing Rohingya land and preventing displaced people from returning to their homes, while allowing non-Rohingya communities to settle on some confiscated properties.Satellite imagery reviewed by the UN indicates that around 2,000 acres of land have been seized. Witness accounts also describe children as young as six being subjected to forced labour.Former detainees have reported torture in custody, with some inmates allegedly dying as a result of their treatment.The abuses have left the Rohingya trapped between competing armed forces, with neither the military nor the Arakan Army providing meaningful protection from persecution and violence.The conflict has also created a parallel economy that is helping finance armed groups while devastating local communities and the environment.The UN report highlights the rapid expansion of illegal rare-earth mining in Kachin and Shan states, where the collapse of the rule of law has allowed illicit industries to flourish.In Kachin, at least 302 new mining sites have emerged since the 2021 coup. In Shan State, the number of sites has increased from just 12 before the coup to 85.The rare-earth trade reached an estimated peak value of $1.4 billion in 2023, with much of the output flowing into China’s market, according to the UN.But the economic gains have come at a devastating environmental and human cost.Toxic chemicals released during mining have contaminated waterways and farmland, contributing to chronic illnesses and reported miscarriages among communities living near mining areas.The pollution is also crossing national borders. Contaminated water has reached rivers flowing into Thailand, where testing has detected elevated levels of arsenic, lead, mercury and manganese.
Article Summary: The human rights situation in Myanmar has reached a new low, with widespread atrocities against the Rohingya minority. Unrelenting conflict, military violence and a growing ‘conflict economy’ have exposed millions of civilians to severe hardship. Both the Myanmar military and the Arakan Army have been accused of systemic abuses against Rohingya communities.
